battle.name: 第二次西西里戰爭
battle.theater: 西西里島東岸敘拉古與埃庇波拉
battle.brief: 公元前415年雅典以一百五十艘三列槳船、二萬五千重裝步兵遠征敘拉古，圍城三年終以全軍覆沒收場。本條目所錄公元前410年屬戰爭收尾階段：阿基比亞德於基齊庫斯得勝，拉凱斯再入西西里未果，敘拉古終成島上霸權。卡面的科林斯青銅盔為重裝步兵方陣的原型裝備，閉目式設計正是遠征軍覆滅的註腳。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 第二次西西里戰爭的交戰方實際上分作四層，並非兩個國家單獨對決。雅典一方是德洛斯同盟的宗主與盟邦領袖：五百人議事會與民會表決出兵，戰役由十將軍委員會執法，最初由尼西亞斯、拉馬庫斯與阿基比亞德三人分掌統帥，議會另撥一千泰連特軍費，艦隊由雅典兩百艘三列槳船中抽調一百五十艘，全軍計有重裝步兵兩萬五千、輕裝兵五千，連同槳手與隨軍工匠合計約四萬人。敘拉古一方是西西里島上的多利安城邦聯盟，以敘拉古為核心，聯結塞利農斯、阿克拉加斯、革拉、希梅拉、卡馬里納等邦，民政由各邦的議會與將軍會議運作，戰時統兵者為赫莫克拉忒與卡馬里納的西卡諾斯，後期由青年狄俄尼索斯率隊夜襲敵營。斯巴達與伯羅奔尼撒同盟屬第三層介入者：國王阿吉斯二世與執政官議決派兵，派遣格勞庫斯率二十艘船西行，之後再以同盟軍身份支援敘拉古圍攻卡馬里納與阿克拉加斯，並與波斯總督法爾納巴佐斯在東地中海協同作戰。幕後的資源方是波斯與迦太基：薩西斯宮廷以軍費餽贈斯巴達，迦太基與敘拉古同屬西地中海貿易圈的盟友，卻在最關鍵的兵員投入上遲疑未決。為雅典作戰的還有利昂提尼、塞格斯塔、埃格斯特與麥西那等西西里盟邦。整場衝突是三種企圖交錯：雅典要打通至西西里的航路與糧道，敘拉古要保住城邦聯盟的主權與西西里航運的壟斷，斯巴達則要證明雅典的帝國並非不可挑戰。
countriesEn: The Second Sicilian War actually involved four layers of belligerents rather than two states settling accounts on their own. On the Athenian side stood the guarantor and leading member of the Delian League: the Council of Five Hundred and the Assembly voted the expedition, the board of ten generals (strategoi) held the command, and the force was originally entrusted to three of them, Nicias, Lamachus and Alcibiades. The Assembly voted a special war levy of one thousand talents, and the fleet was drawn at one hundred and fifty triremes out of the two hundred Athens had; the army counted twenty-five thousand hoplites and five thousand light-armed, and roughly forty thousand men in all once oarsmen, craftsmen and camp followers were added. On the Syracusan side was the league of the Doric city-states of Sicily, centred on Syracuse and joined to Selinus, Acragas, Gela, Himera and Camarina, each city governed by its own councils and assemblies of Siceliots; the field commanders were Hermocrates and Sicanus of Camarina, and in the later phase the young Dionysius the Elder led the night attack on the enemy camp. The third layer was the intervention of Sparta and the Peloponnesian League: after the kings and the ephors had debated the matter, Gylippus was sent west with twenty ships, and the League afterwards supported Syracuse in the sieges of Camarina and Acragas and fought alongside the Persian satrap Pharnabazus in the eastern Mediterranean. The behind-the-scenes suppliers were Persia and Carthage: the court of Sardis paid money to Sparta, and Carthage, an ally of Syracuse inside the western Mediterranean trade system, hesitated over the one commitment of troops that would really have mattered. Athens also fought with Sicilian allies such as Leontini, Segesta, Egesta and Messana. What the war actually joined together were three designs that pulled in different directions: Athens wanted a lane and a grain route into Sicily, Syracuse wanted to preserve the sovereignty of the Sicilian league and its monopoly of Sicilian shipping, and Sparta wanted to prove that the Athenian empire could be beaten.
people: 關鍵人物集中在少數人身上，多數以演說而非武藝左右戰局。出征之前，尼西亞斯在民會上以疾病蔓延與準備不足為由反對遠征；他是三人中年長而富於資歷者，最終仍被推舉為統帥之一，並在兵敗之後主持了那場艱難的撤退。拉馬庫斯是三人中唯一以兵略見長者，他主張以主動出擊取代封鎖港區的穩守，在埃庇波拉高地築成既能俯瞰海港又可自守的營地，公元前414年陣亡於敘拉古方面的伏擊。阿基比亞德的作為決定了戰爭的走向：他在民會上推動遠征，向城邦許諾只需一日航程便可把西西里收入版圖；遠征開始前他因赫爾墨斯石像被毀一案被放逐，隨即倒向斯巴達，再轉投波斯總督提薩斐內斯，在西西里戰局最危急時建議斯巴達出兵干預並切斷雅典的海上生命線；公元前410年他重獲軍權，在赫勒斯滂的基齊庫斯海戰中以奇襲大敗斯巴達與波斯的聯合艦隊。敘拉古方面以赫莫克拉忒為首，他既是指揮官也是全城最傑出的辯士，在卡馬里納議會上的演說促成島內各邦合縱，戰局逆轉後又主持對雅典營地的夜襲與正面進攻，兵敗後隨和約返國。斯巴達將軍格勞庫斯以少量船隊抵達即扭轉戰局，先後圍困卡馬里納與阿克拉加斯，最終在後來的敘拉古圍城戰中病逝；青年狄俄尼索斯參與夜襲而嶄露頭角，日後成為西西里最有力量的統治者。
peopleEn: The decisive personalities were few, and most of them shaped the war by oratory rather than by arms. Before the expedition sailed, Nicias opposed it in the Assembly on the grounds of disease and inadequate preparation; he was the oldest and most experienced of the three and was nevertheless pressed into command, and it was he who later conducted the miserable retreat after the defeat. Lamachus was the only one of the three with a real record in fieldcraft: he argued for active operations in place of a passive blockade of the harbour, built a camp on the high ground of Epipolae that could both overlook the sea and be defended, and was killed in an ambush by the Syracusans in 414 BC. Alcibiades' actions decided the course of the war. In the Assembly he pushed the expedition forward on a promise that Sicily lay a single day's sail away and could be folded into the Athenian empire; before the fleet sailed he was ostracised after the mutilation of the Hermai, went over to Sparta and then to the Persian satrap Tissaphernes, and at the crisis of the Sicilian war urged Sparta to intervene and to cut the maritime lifeline of Athens; in 410 BC he was restored to command and destroyed a combined Spartan and Persian fleet by a surprise attack at Cyzicus in the Hellespont. On the Syracusan side the leading figure was Hermocrates, a commander who was also the finest speaker in the city: his speech in the assembly of Camarina helped unite the Sicilian cities, and after the tide turned he directed the night attack and the frontal assault on the Athenian camp, returning home after the peace. The Spartan general Gylippus turned the war with a handful of ships, besieged Camarina and then Acragas, and was ultimately killed by the plague in the later siege of Syracuse; the young Dionysius, who took part in the night attack and showed his mettle, went on to become the strongest ruler in Sicily.
kits: 卡面這頂科林斯青銅盔是希臘重裝步兵全副武裝的原型：眼孔狹窄、面甲全開，戴上之後視野只剩正前方一條縫，行動、號令與呼吸全靠身旁的同伴，因此它的價值不在防禦而在維持方陣。須說明的是，公元前650年前後定型的那種全覆面科林斯盔，到公元前415年早已不合用：雅典出發的精銳重裝步兵已改用眼孔較闊、露出耳鼻的阿提卡盔（Attic），稍後又被切爾基迪亞盔取代，全覆面的科林斯盔只在科林斯本地與部分老兵、傭兵手中仍可見到。科林斯是敘拉古的母邦城，公元前734年建城，敘拉古的多利安制度與裝備仍帶著科林斯的樣子，這頂盔的形制基因也就始終留在島上防守方的方陣裡。就這場戰爭的實際配備而言，遠征軍的重裝步兵裝備圓盾、青銅盔、護脛與長矛，矛尾可拆的青銅尾槍使矛既能刺擊也能放平拖行；部分人穿麻布胸甲（linothorax），胸甲下綴皮條，護腿僅及膝下。修昔底德記錄了雙方裝備的細節：西刻里俄提人的武裝最為齊整，其餘西西里人用輕便的柳條盾與可投擲的短柄矛，敘拉古與其餘希臘盟軍則是全副希臘式裝備。攻城方面，雅典人帶來可移動的撞盾與撞槌、挖向牆基的坑道與試圖築棧橋登陸的器械；敘拉古人以火船攻擊泊在港內的戰船，並在海峽橫切一道城牆，把敵營封死在陸地上。運輸與糧秣方面，一百五十艘三列槳船要供應越過愛奧尼亞海、沿海南下的航程與每日食糧，一旦離開母邦港口，糧食便要靠島上的塞利農斯接濟。
kitsEn: The Corinthian bronze helmet on the card is the archetype of the full panoply of the Greek hoplite: the eye slits are narrow and the face plate covers everything, so that once it is on, the wearer can see only a slot straight ahead, and movement, orders and breathing all depend on the men at his shoulders. It has to be said that the fully enclosing Corinthian helmet as it was fixed in type around 650 BC was already long obsolete by 415 BC: the elite hoplites who sailed from Athens wore the Attic helmet with wider openings that left the ears and nose clear, and were later displaced by the Chalcidian type; the fully enclosing Corinthian shell survived only in Corinth itself and in the hands of some older soldiers and mercenaries. Corinth was the mother city of Syracuse, founded in 734 BC, and the Doric institutions and equipment of Syracuse still carried a Corinthian look, so the formal genes of this helmet remained inside the phalanx that defended the island. As for the actual equipment of this war: the hoplites of the expedition carried the round shield, a bronze helmet, greaves and a spear whose detachable bronze butt-spike allowed it to be used for a thrust or dragged flat behind a runner; some wore the linen cuirass (linothorax) with its leather pteruges hanging below, and greaves reaching only below the knee. Thucydides records the details on both sides: the Siceliots had the best armour of all, the other Sicilians made do with light wicker shields and javelins, and Syracuse and the rest of the Hellenic allies fought in full Greek kit. On the siege side the Athenians brought mobile shield-batteries and rams, tunnels driven at the foot of the wall and the means of trying to bridge a landing; the Syracusans answered with fire-ships against the warships lying in the harbour and with a wall cut across the strait that sealed the enemy camp in on the land. In the matter of transport and supply, a hundred and fifty triremes had to feed the crossing of the Ionian Sea, the coastwise run southwards and the daily rations of the army; once the fleet left the ports of the mother city, the food had to be drawn from Sicily itself, chiefly from Selinus.
tactics: 戰術層面上，這是一場以海軍投射、以重裝步兵結陣的攻城戰，而它的失敗幾乎每一步都寫在修昔底德的記載裡。公元前415年夏，萊普蒂涅斯率二十餘艘三列槳船夜入大港，焚燒對岸泊船並登岸破壞一段城牆，卻沒能奪取港口本身；隨後拉馬庫斯在埃庇波拉高地建立營地，雅典人築起「歐律羅斯圓牆」，把海角與高地包成一座封閉的堡壘，一度把敘拉古壓在海港與陸路之間。敘拉古的赫莫克拉忒卻從海峽另一側築起一道與圓牆平行的反牆，並在牆基下方掘進坑道，使雅典的攻城器材無法靠近；公元前414年，敘拉古在退潮時自高地向圓牆內的營地發動反擊，擊殺拉馬庫斯，迫使遠征軍放棄埃庇波拉。格勞庫斯的援軍帶來制海權後，敘拉古得以從陸海兩面夾擊。公元前413年，雅典的兩路援軍在普列米里翁角的海戰中敗於約八十艘對六十艘的艦隊，達摩斯梯尼的採礦大軍在阿伊吉納淺灘上因勞動隊伍與船隊遭突擊而全軍覆沒；撤退中的遠征軍在安納普斯河上游遭敘拉古軍封堵，僅約三千人突圍。最終是海峽橫牆合攏，加上營中饑疫與攻方器械的耗盡，令整支遠征軍在城郊投降。
tacticsEn: At the level of tactics this was a siege fought by naval projection and by a phalanx of hoplites, and its failure is written down almost step by step in Thucydides. In the summer of 415 BC Leptines took rather more than twenty triremes into the Great Harbour at night, burned the ships moored on the far side and landed to destroy a stretch of the city wall, but did not take the harbour itself; Lamachus then raised his camp on the high ground of Epipolae, and the Athenians built the 'circular wall of Euryelus', enclosing the promontory and the heights in a closed fortress and for a time squeezing Syracuse between the harbour and the land road. Hermocrates of Syracuse answered by raising a counter-wall parallel to the circular wall from the far side of the strait and driving tunnels beneath the foot of it so that the Athenian siege works could not be brought up; in 414 BC the Syracusans attacked downhill at low water onto the camp inside the wall, killed Lamachus and forced the expedition to abandon Epipolae. Once Gylippus' reinforcements brought sea control, Syracuse could close in from the land and the water at the same time. In 413 BC the two Athenian reliefs were beaten in the naval action off the Plemmyrium by a fleet of about eighty ships against sixty, and Demosthenes' mining army was destroyed on the shoal of Aegina when the working parties and the fleet were caught by a surprise attack; the retreating expedition was cut off on the upper reaches of the Anapus and only about three thousand men broke through. What finished it was the closing of the wall across the strait, together with hunger and sickness in the camp and the exhaustion of the siege equipment: the whole expedition surrendered on the outskirts of the city.
data: 可核對的數字集中在四處。遠征軍的編制最常被引述：公元前415年出航時是一百五十艘三列槳船、二萬五千名重裝步兵與五千名輕裝兵，若連同槳手與隨軍人員，總兵力約四萬人，專款軍費一千泰連特；遠征主力的營地只留三百名重裝步兵看守，其餘主力沿海轉進。兵敗時的損失同樣有數：普列米里翁海戰中雅典遠征艦隊六十艘對上敘拉古方面的約八十艘，達摩斯梯尼在阿伊吉納淺灘的勞動大軍約五千人殉難或被俘，五十艘船盡失；安納普斯河一役後，六千餘人被俘並於次年被處決，另有約七千人被關在城外石坑（latomia）裏做苦役，遠征軍自此再無成建制的部隊回國。戰爭的另一半數字在海峽：公元前410年基齊庫斯海戰中雅典聯軍俘獲約八百人，敵方艦隊與波斯陸上大營同潰，隨即組建由拉凱斯率領、二十艘船的西西里分遣隊。戰線的地面跨度不大：從埃庇波拉高地的營地到大港南端的普列米里翁角，圍城的兩道平行牆連同海峽橫牆首尾相望；島上各邦的背叛則讓戰局在數月之間從僵持變成崩潰。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked are concentrated in four places. The composition of the expedition is the most often quoted: when it sailed in 415 BC there were one hundred and fifty triremes, twenty-five thousand hoplites and five thousand light-armed, about forty thousand men in all once the oarsmen and the auxiliaries were counted, and a special war levy of one thousand talents; only three hundred hoplites were left to hold the main camp while the rest of the army moved on along the coast. The losses are equally documented: in the action off the Plemmyrium the Athenian expeditionary fleet of sixty ships met about eighty Syracusan ships, Demosthenes' mining force of about five thousand men was killed or captured on the shoal of Aegina and fifty triremes were lost; after the fighting on the Anapus more than six thousand men were taken and killed the following year, while some seven thousand more were shut up in the stone quarries (latomia) outside the city, and from then on not one organised body of the expedition ever returned to Athens. The other set of numbers belongs to the Hellespont: in the battle of Cyzicus in 410 BC the Athenian allies captured about eight hundred men, the enemy fleet and the Persian camp on shore collapsed together, and a squadron of twenty ships under Laches was raised for Sicily. The ground span of the fighting was short: from the camp on the heights of Epipolae to the Plemmyrium at the southern mouth of the Great Harbour, the two parallel siege walls and the wall across the strait lay within sight of one another; and the defection of the Sicilian cities turned a stalemate into a collapse within a few months.
cause: 打起來的原因有遠因也有近因，兩者互相咬合。遠因是公元前418年的尼西亞斯和約只讓伯羅奔尼撒戰爭停了下來，沒有一個結構性問題被解決：德洛斯同盟的盟邦在稅負與訴訟上不斷申辯，雅典帝國靠同盟繳交的貢金維持，而那片帝國的西部邊界從未真正劃定。前一年在米洛斯島上，雅典使者的演說已向全希臘宣告過：帝國的邊界遠比想像中脆弱。西西里提供了三種誘惑：塞格斯塔與埃格斯特的使節帶著「同盟遭欺凌」的說法前來求援，實際的物質利益極少，卻提供了合法的出兵藉口；利昂提尼與敘拉古之間關於溫泉地帶（Thermae）邊界與西刻里俄提人歸屬的糾紛，給了雅典干預的理由；而西西里島本身的糧食、船隻與商路，是任何一個地中海強權都不會放手的資源。近因在雅典內部：阿基比亞德需要一場屬於自己的戰事來鞏固地位，尼西亞斯則以風險過大便以退為進，兩人在民會上把遠征說成一件必然成功、只需一日航行就能完成的事；議事會在節慶期間以不足法定人數通過了開戰與撥款的決議，遠征因此從一場倉促的賭注變成國家政策。遠征開始前的「赫爾墨斯石像被毀」一案把阿基比亞德送入放逐，隨即引來斯巴達的干預，敘拉古由此得到科林斯與島內盟邦的援助而站穩陣腳，原本孤注一擲的遠征，於是變成兩個帝國爭奪西西里的持久戰。
causeEn: There were distant causes and immediate ones, and the two were welded together. The distant cause is that the peace of Nicias in 418 BC only paused the Peloponnesian War without settling a single structural problem: the allies of the Delian League kept protesting about the tribute and the courts, the Athenian empire was maintained by the money the allies paid in, and the western edge of that empire had never actually been drawn. The year before, on the island of Melos, the speeches of the Athenian envoys had already announced to all Greece that the borders of the empire were far more fragile than imagined. Sicily offered three kinds of temptation: the envoys of Segesta and Egesta came asking for help on the pretext that their allies had been wronged, offering very little material substance but providing a legitimate pretext for intervention; the quarrel between Leontini and Syracuse over the borderland of the hot springs (Thermae) and over the allegiance of the Sicelians gave Athens a reason to meddle; and the grain, the shipping and the trade of the island itself were resources no Mediterranean power would willingly give up. The immediate cause lay inside Athens: Alcibiades needed a war of his own to consolidate his position, while Nicias used the excessive risk as a reason to give ground, and the two of them sold the expedition in the Assembly as a thing certain to succeed and finished in a single day's sail; the Council, sitting during the festival season and short of a legal quorum, passed the declarations of war and of the levy, and the expedition therefore hardened from a rash gamble into a policy of the state. The mutilation of the Hermai before the fleet sailed sent Alcibiades into exile, brought the intervention of Sparta, and gave Syracuse the help of Corinth and of the Sicilian allies, so that a throw-of-the-dice raid turned into a long war between two empires for the possession of Sicily.
impact: 失敗的後果遠超出西西里本身。雅典失去的是帝國的信用：遠征軍的覆沒讓全希臘看見同盟的軍隊也可以被一支防守的城市軍隊摧毀，隨後的斯巴達進攻得以在沒有任何盟邦援助的情況下直抵雅典城下；公元前411年的四百人會議與前410年的五千人會議，說明帝國崩解的同時，雅典的政體也已分裂到底。公元前404年雅典投降後，愛琴海與西西里不再是兩個可以分開的問題：西部的強權與東部的海權必須在同一個聯盟裡彼此讓步，斯巴達的霸權在戰後數十年內被雅典主導的第二提洛同盟取代，而西西里則交給了敘拉古。對西西里島本身，敘拉古的勝利把一個聯盟式的多利安邦聯變成以城邦為中心的霸權秩序：狄俄尼索斯一世在公元前405年取得政權後，把島上的稅收與兵力集中到敘拉古，造船、築城、鑄造帶著城邦徽記的銀幣，並在公元前405年之後逐一清理先前獨立的城邦，希梅拉在公元前406年被迦太基軍在狄俄尼索斯部的配合下毀滅，塞利農斯在公元前397年被狄俄尼索斯本人攻毀而居民被遷走，往後百餘年西西里與迦太基的角力，底子是在這場戰爭之後奠下的。對海軍技術與戰術思想而言，敘拉古守住海峽的戰役也示範了什麼：艦隊要能封鎖海峽，也要在城牆之間的灘地上頂住對方的登陸；遠征軍的教訓則被寫進此後所有希臘將領的算計裡。
impactEn: The consequences of the defeat reached far beyond Sicily. What Athens lost was the credit of its empire: the destruction of the expedition showed all Greece that an allied army could be broken by the garrison of a single city, and the subsequent Spartan advance could reach the walls of Athens without the help of a single ally; the Council of Four Hundred in 411 BC and the Council of Five Thousand in 410 BC showed that the polity of Athens had broken down at the same time as the empire. After Athens surrendered in 404 BC, the Aegean and Sicily were no longer two separate problems: the power in the west and the sea power in the east had to accommodate each other inside one league, the Spartan hegemony was replaced within a few decades by the second Delian League led by Athens, and Sicily was handed over to Syracuse. For Sicily itself, the victory of Syracuse turned a federal league of Doric cities into a hegemonic order centred on one city: after taking power in 405 BC, Dionysius the Elder concentrated the island's revenues and manpower in Syracuse, building ships and walls, striking silver coins that carried the city's emblem, and, after 405 BC, picking off the cities that had been independent before; Himera was destroyed in 406 BC by a Carthaginian army operating with the help of Dionysius' troops, Selinus was taken by Dionysius himself in 397 BC and its inhabitants moved out, and the long struggle between Sicily and Carthage over the following century was founded on what was settled in this war. For naval technique and for tactical thought, the defence of the strait by Syracuse also demonstrated something: a fleet has to be able to seal a strait and has to hold the shore between two walls against a landing; and the lesson of the expedition was written into the calculations of every Hellenic commander after that.
result: 打完了的結果是：公元前413年，遠征軍在安納普斯河上游全軍投降，尼西亞斯與達摩斯梯尼被押回雅典處死，約六千名俘虜在敘拉古的公民大會上被殺，約七千人被囚於城外石坑；塞利農斯、革拉、希梅拉等城邦隨之倒向敘拉古，西西里聯盟在數年之內成為以敘拉古為核心的體系。雅典失去的不只是一支遠征軍：公元前411年城邦內部的政變與對外戰線的失敗互相放大，斯巴達海軍取得愛琴海的制海權，最終在公元前404年迫使雅典投降，長達二十七年的伯羅奔尼撒戰爭以雅典帝國的終結作結。戰爭的尾巴還拖了很久：公元前410年雅典在赫勒斯滂的基齊庫斯取勝，拉凱斯率二十艘船再入西西里，試圖重燃戰火，卻在沒有兵力支持的情況下被召回；公元前405年敘拉古與斯巴達聯軍圍攻島上雅典殘部與西刻里俄提人的戰事中，狄俄尼索斯一世以夜襲奪下城內的雅典堡壘，切斷守軍的外援，斯巴達將軍格勞庫斯則在城內病逝，圍城因疫情與兵力耗盡而中止。西西里島從此再沒有足以與敘拉古抗衡的第二勢力，直到坎尼戰役之後羅馬的介入，才改寫這座島的命運。
resultEn: The result was this: in 413 BC the expedition surrendered with all arms on the upper Anapus, Nicias and Demosthenes were dragged back to Athens and executed, about six thousand prisoners were killed by the assembly of Syracuse, and some seven thousand more were shut up in the stone quarries outside the city; Selinus, Gela, Himera and the other cities went over to Syracuse, and within a few years the Sicilian league had become a system centred on Syracuse. Athens had lost more than an army: the coups inside the city in 411 BC and the collapse of the external front reinforced one another, the Spartan navy took command of the Aegean, and by 404 BC Athens was forced to surrender, and the Peloponnesian War, which had run for twenty-seven years, ended with the end of the Athenian empire. The tail of the war dragged on for a long time. In 410 BC Athens won at Cyzicus in the Hellespont and Laches took twenty ships back into Sicily in an attempt to rekindle the war, only to be recalled without the means to sustain it; in the siege of the Athenian remnant in Syracuse in 405 BC, Dionysius the Elder took the Athenian fort inside the city by night assault and cut the garrison off from outside help, while the Spartan general Gylippus died of the plague inside the walls and the siege was abandoned as the sickness and the losses of both sides mounted. From then on Sicily had no second power capable of holding its own against Syracuse, and it took the intervention of Rome after the battle of Cannae to change the island's fortunes.
